title: Understanding KDE
text: A Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) is a way to estimate the probability density function of a random variable. It involves placing a kernel, which is a smooth, symmetric function, at each data point.

title: Normalization in KDE
text: Normalization ensures that each kernel contributes equally to the overall density estimate. This is typically done by ensuring each kernel has an area of $$1$$.

hintAnswer: Each kernel has an area of $$1$$
title: Choosing the Correct Normalization
text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the normalization of kernels in a KDE?
choices: Each kernel has an area of \alpha
Each kernel has an area of $$1$$
The total area under the KDE curve is $$1$$
